original_claim.title: Trump Pressures NSC Official Who Warned Cultural Site Bombing Was a War Crime
original_claim.synopsis: After Trump publicly threatened to strike Iranian cultural sites in January 2020, at least one National Security Council official internally warned the president that such strikes would violate international law and constitute war crimes under the laws of armed conflict. According to reports, the official faced pressure and retribution for raising these legal objections — consistent with a broader pattern in the Trump administration of punishing officials who provided inconvenient legal or factual guidance. The episode illustrates how Trump's inner circle was forced to choose between institutional loyalty to lawful conduct and personal loyalty to the president's stated intent. Senior military and legal advisors were left in the position of quietly cleaning up after presidential threats that violated US treaty obligations.

identified_problems.explanation: Trump publicly threatened Iranian cultural sites in January 2020 and Defense Secretary Mark Esper publicly stated that U.S. forces would follow the laws of armed conflict. I did not verify the entry's specific allegation that an NSC official who privately warned such strikes would be war crimes was pressured or retaliated against.

original_claim.title: Iran Retaliates with Ballistic Missiles at US Bases in Middle East
original_claim.synopsis: Within 48 hours of the US-Israeli airstrikes on its nuclear facilities, Iran launched salvos of ballistic missiles targeting US military installations across the Middle East in June 2025. The strikes hit bases in Iraq, Qatar, and the UAE, injuring dozens of US service members and killing at least three. Iran used its Shahab-3 and Emad medium-range ballistic missiles, which US and allied missile defense systems only partially intercepted. The retaliatory strikes forced the evacuation of non-essential personnel from several bases and triggered emergency calls between Trump and allied leaders. The episode demonstrated that the military strikes on Iran's nuclear facilities had not eliminated Iran's conventional military capability to threaten US forces.

original_claim.title: Pam Bondi DOJ Drops All Pending Cases Against Trump Allies on Day One
original_claim.synopsis: On January 20, 2025, within hours of her confirmation as Attorney General, Pam Bondi directed the DOJ to drop all pending federal cases against Trump associates and allies, including cases that had been brought by career prosecutors following the January 6 investigation and other matters. The mass dismissal of cases bypassed normal DOJ review processes and was carried out without explanation of the merits. Career DOJ prosecutors who had worked the cases for years described the action as politically motivated and legally unjustifiable. The move was characterized by former officials as an unprecedented purge of legitimate prosecutions for purely political purposes, effectively ending DOJ independence as a check on presidential power.

On April 24, the White House directed the Attorney General to investigate allegations involving straw-donor and foreign contributions through online fundraising platforms. Separately, the FEC recorded a 4–0 vote on April 29 dismissing specified reporting allegations involving Trump committees. The first is a directive to investigate; the second is an FEC decision, not a DOJ prosecution. Neither proves or disproves a department-wide selective-enforcement policy.
